newsitem.title: USA: Analyst sees lower U.S. gas prices in medium term.
newsitem.headline: Analyst sees lower U.S. gas prices in medium term.

text.p: Goldman Sachs analyst Donald Textor on Tuesday said he sees domestic natural gas prices in the $2.10-$2.20 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu) range over the next 24 to 36 months, down from this year's estimated $2.50 mmBtu range.
Electric utilities will continue to exert downward pressure on natural gas prices by switching to other fuels when gas prices rise too steeply, Textor said.
"You've got to keep electricity in the game," Textor said in a speech to a group of independent oil and natural gas producers in Houston.
Longer term, a 2 percent annual growth in domestic gas demand and stepped up production from deepwater wells in the Gulf of Mexico should keep the market in balance, he said.
Production from 18 deepwater projects announced publicly should rise to 2.15 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) in 1999 from 262 mmcfd last year, Textor said.
The estimates do not include another 18 discoveries that have not been announced publicly, he said. "These numbers should continue to rise well into the future," he said.
